record_type_quote: To this end, we conducted a direct replication of a recent, often-cited study of threat appeals, using the same methods as the original investigation.

targets.authors: Skurka, C., Niederdeppe, J., Romero-Canyas, R., & Acup, D.
targets.title: Pathways of influence in emotional appeals: Benefits and tradeoffs of using fear or humor to promote climate change-related intentions and risk perceptions.
targets.evidence_quote: To this end, we present the results from a preregistered, direct replication of Skurka et al. (2018).
targets.outcome_quote: Using the same stimuli, measures, and experimental design with a similar sample, we fail to replicate these main effects. We do, however, replicate age as a moderator of humor’s effect on perceived risk, such that the humor appeal only persuaded emerging adults (ages 18-21.9).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Main effects failed, but the age moderation of perceived risk replicated. The authors distinguish the failed fear induction from the disconfirming humor findings; they do not declare the whole attempt uninformative.

reasoning: Identity and authors verified in accepted manuscript; full article including references. New sample directly re-tests one published paper.
